session_note: third session, continued from s3-c1c2; cycle 4 is a promotion-role replay of the disputed steps=21-vs-42 held_out comparison, this time with both arms fully completing the suite under PR #1253's completion gate

cross_session_resolution.claim: This is the first observed run of this nominal 'cycle 4' recipe where BOTH arms fully complete held_out (5/5 each) -- every prior observation (#1246, #1248, session-2/#1250) had the control arm complete only 1/5. With full completion on both sides, held_out.structural_similarity is control=0.38248 -> candidate=0.37006, a REGRESSION (-0.0124), numerically identical to PR #1247's measurement (which also reported control=0.38248).
cross_session_resolution.resolution: The disagreement documented in docs/design/continuous-openui-20260801-s2-c4-results.md and model-build-partial-suite-completion-gate-20260801.md is now resolved: #1247's regression finding was correct; #1248's 'positive' claim and session 2's numerically-matching replication were both artifacts of the control arm only completing 1/5 held_out documents (giving an artificially low control value of 0.3417 that made steps=42 look like an improvement). Doubling steps does NOT improve held_out.structural_similarity at this recipe -- it is a real, small regression once both arms are measured on a comparable (fully-completed) basis.
cross_session_resolution.recommendation: PRs #1246 and #1248 should not be treated as ship-relevant positive evidence for the steps=42 lever; #1247's regression finding is the trustworthy one. No further stacking on the steps=42 direction from this recipe.
